title: Severe disseminated Talaromyces marneffei infection in idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia
case_text:
A previously healthy man in his 40 s was referred for a 15-day history of fever, headache, fatigue, vomiting, poor appetite. He had been treated with antibiotics 10 days prior, but without any improvement in his symptoms. Upon admission, vital signs included a body temperature of 38.9 C, respiration of 20 breaths/min, heart rate at 116 beats/min, blood pressure of 130/82 mmHg, and O2 saturation of 98 % on ambient air. Physical examination revealed mild jaundice of the sclera and skin, along with significant enlargement of the liver and spleen.
Laboratory tests results are as follows: white blood cell count of 6.87 x 109 /L (normal, 3.5-9.5 x109 /L), with neutrophils 93 % (40-75 %), total bilirubin 33.9 mumol/L (0-21 mumol/L), direct bilirubin 28.7 mumol/L (0-6.8 mumol/L), alaninetransaminase 132 U/L (13-40 U/L), aspartate aminotransferase 227 U/L (7-45 U/L), high-sensitive c-reactive protein 110.2 mg/L (0-5 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate 19 mm/h (0-20 mm/h). A computed tomography (CT) scan revealed an irregular mass in the lateral segment of the right middle lobe of the lung with a size of 3.7 x 3.0 x 3.2 cm, and enlargement of the liver and spleen with multiple low-density lesions (Fig. 1A, B). Therefore lung, liver and spleen punctures were performed. The lung puncture revealed sausage-like shapes yeast organisms with midline septum (Fig. 1C). Mycological cultures from blood, bone marrow, liver and spleen were positive for TM.
However, Thorough investigations showed no evidence of HIV infection, autoimmune disease, the use of immunosuppressive drugs, and malignancies. Further immunodeficiency evaluation was conducted. Serum immunoglobulin levels showed normal IgG level of 9.61 g/L (8.6-17.4 g/L), IgA level of 1.2 g/L (1-4.2 g/L), IgM level of 0.58 g/L (0.3-2.2 g/L), and elevated IgE level of 318.4 IU/ml (0-100 IU/ml). Complement levels were decreased, with C3 at 0.52 (0.7-1.4 mg/dL) and C4 0.09 (0.1-0.4 mg/dL). Flow cytometry assay revealed reduced CD4 T-cell at 12.66 % (30-46 %) with a count of 32 (561-1137), CD8 T-cell at 20 % (19.2-33.6 %) with a count of 50 (220-1030), B cell at 3 % (8.5-14.5 %) and NK cell at 2.14 % (9.5-23.5 %). Serum anti-interferon-gamma autoantibodies testing was negative. Thus, a diagnosis of disseminated TM infection due to ICL was established.

You are an expert clinician–educator in tropical and infectious diseases.
Your job is to transform a published clinical case report into a standardized admission diagnostic teaching case following the Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology.

In terms of style, model your output on NEJM’s Clinicopathologic Conferences ("Case Records of the Massachusetts General Hospital").

RULES (Read Carefully — No Exceptions):
1. SOURCE FIDELITY:
   - Extract facts ONLY from the supplied case report.
   - Do NOT invent, embellish, or smooth out missing clinical data.
   - Never extrapolate findings not explicitly mentioned.

2. THE ADMISSION BREAKPOINT PRINCIPLE (CRITICAL):
   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Talaromycosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: disseminated Talaromyces marneffei infection in idiopathic CD4 lymphopenia
